events.title: Domestic Gas Reservation Scheme law passed: exporters must supply up to 20% of annual export volumes to the domestic market from 1 Jan 2028

key_dates.label: Export licensing framework intended to start

materiality.basis: Reserves up to 20% of export volumes for the domestic market; the ABC reports the policy aims to oversupply the domestic market to push prices down

directness.basis: Applies to the class 'gas exporters'; the companies are not named in the source

events.reasoning: A binding domestic supply obligation on east-coast exporters can lower the price they realise on reserved volumes. The impact depends on licence terms that are not set yet, and the obligation starts in 2028.

notes: Passage date: DISR says 27 Nov 2026; ABC reported the Senate vote on the evening of 26 Nov. Check the Senate Journals.
Which listed companies hold export licences, and their volumes, is not in the source.

notes: Passage date: DISR says 27 Nov 2026; ABC reported the Senate vote on the evening of 26 Nov. Check the Senate Journals.
Woodside's east-coast export exposure, if any, needs checking.
